text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The government is urging the European Union to speed up negotiations for a commercial agreement on textile and garment export quotas.
-- The government is attempting to trace and reward the wartime efforts of over one million youth volunteers who served during the period 1946-1975.
-- Vice minister of Science, Technology and Environment Chu Hao said Internet operations will start in Vietnam later this month.
-- Ho Chi Minh City party chief Truong Tan Sang has called for party units and the authorities to boost hunger eradication and poverty alleviation programmes.
-- Vietnam reported an estimated trade deficit of $1.433 billion in the first half of this year.
-- The spring-winter paddy crop has reached 13.2 million tonnes, up by 8.5 percent from last year's harvest.
-- Construction of a $185 million urban area in the outskirts of Hanoi will start in July.
-- Vietnam's child protection committee has called for stronger efforts by local authorities to reduce the numbers of street children in major cities.
-- 78,000 jobs were created in Ho Chi Minh City during the first six months of 1997. The current unemployment rate is 6.7 percent.
-- Garment and textile exports to the European Union amounted to $157 million between January 1 and May 31, up 42 percent from the same period last year.
